doc.title: Percy Humphrey Band: Percy Humphrey, Jim Robinson, Ernest Roubleau, Josiah Frazier Interview, 1972-02-29

chapter: Army service in World War I
title: Learning trombone in the army band in France
summary: Jim tells how an officer, Lieutenant Lion, took him on and taught him trombone, and the band played around France.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Yeah. on his hands, came on with the band, was a good position. And William Foster, you know, all the people, you know. And William Foster said, Bob, you called me Bob, he said, he said, let's come and get the band with us, with the lines. And they brought all them boys, put them on nice, put them shoes, rustling shoes, tanned shoes, they brought them heavy shoes, with them nails on. William said, I can help you. And he said, yeah, Bob. And so they talked to Lieutenant Lyons, I said, Lord have mercy that morning. They said, anyone who want to take a chance to want to want to let trombone step two two pairs forward. I walked up, I said, Jesus have mercy, don't let me follow this line. What they did. But see, I've been putting my brother trombone playing very trombone, understand. I can make the scale, understand. So I said, listen, Bob, I'm a lanyard. So Luke on the line was a very nice man. He said, he said, well, Ralphson, I said, listen, I'm going to put you on a study. He said, now, with that band, that big band, and them guys playing trombone more than the head, and I said, that was nausea in me, understand. That was nausea in me. I said, oh, no, no, I said, it was nausea. I said, listen. And Ernst and I could play trombone, play trumpet, play trombone too. And Ernst and I told Luther the Lion, I said, listen, I'll tell you what I'll do. I'll take Ralphson. He said, Ralphson won't let the trombone. He said, if you give me, say, but, say, but, but three months with him, I'm going to have him playing. And that's true. And man, just, they wouldn't get me to the YMCA where they're playing, they kept me, down the hill, you know what I'm saying. I said, have my hand against the trombone. And he got me running my skills. And I'll tell you after that person, he started getting me together, I said, you know what I'm saying, I'm going to, I can't be no dumb fool. I'm going to learn something about commercial army. And he just took me. And we started playing, working with the band, made a eight piece band. You know what I'm saying, after I started getting that in France, that cash money, the pen, Luther, the, the, the officer was paying, money for us to play, you understand. But the buck probably used to pay us more than officers, you understand. Because sometimes we, we have to do things, this, some, you see, have all them pretty girls, this, that, that, that, that, that, that. And so, the buck probably getting a good dance, but I'm like, oh man, ooh, all them soldier boys in there, you all come, new tenants, come up there. The buck boy, I said, you can't, boy, boy, that's a mess. What, what, what, no, you can't, yeah. And so, Lieutenant Lion said, this is my band, I can't, little, little Lion said, this is my band, I'll bring watch out. And so the father said, Lieutenant Lion's come on, boy, he's a good lieutenant too, man. Because he had done dressed me up, and had me all cleaned up there, and bought me another clean suit. I was all nasty and dirty, and they got me fixed up. And, you know what I'm saying, every week, he had us going to different places in France, every different place in France. And, and I said, you know what I'm saying, and I started getting them big old francs, I had some big old dollar bills like that, but it get rotten in your pocket, you know what I'm saying, old francs money. Get rotten in your pocket. I said, let's do one thing. And, and, and so, Luther said, let's use change that money. You see, he got told, he got told, right, he said, let you do, say, Ralph, put your money in the YMC. Well that's what I did. And when I, when I got the service, that's true. I had a good batch of money to save up, that's true. That's why you got started on that trunk. Eh? No, listen, wait, no, no, listen, listen, listen, the brothers, we left best friends, and came to Newport News, I mean, North of Virginia. Newport News, Virginia? Eh?
